messages:
maya: Heads up — we need to scope regional/zone dashboards for the new routing policies. Main asks: latency by region, cross-region failover impact, and traffic-split metrics. Who can own telemetry inputs from runtime/infra?

sam: I can take the runtime side. Will need: per-region p50/p90/p99, request counts, KV cache hit rate by region, and a signal for model-variant fallbacks. Also need tags: region, zone, pool, model_variant, routing_policy.

maya: perfect. Can you list exact metric names you plan to emit? product wants rows in the console that map directly to panels.

sam: initial metric names (working):
```
redwood.request.latency_ms{region, zone, model_variant}
redwood.request.count{region, zone, routing_policy}
redwood.kvcache.hit_ratio{region, zone}
redwood.routing.fallback_count{region, zone, from_variant, to_variant}
redwood.routing.traffic_split_percentage{region, pool, target_variant}
redwood.failover.events{region, from_zone, to_zone, trigger}
```
I'll instrument runtime to emit these with 10s scrape resolution.

priya: From SRE: include error rate and overload signals too. We want a per-region overload counter and active queue length per worker pool. Failover impact should show spike in latency and error rate for both origin and target regions. Also add a boolean alert metric for cross-region fallback so oncall can see exact time windows.

alex: UX note — product asks for two views: 1) live operations: single-region micro-panels (latency, QPS, errors, cache) and 2) cross-region comparison heatmap with a time selector + an interactive traffic-split slider that can simulate weighted splits to estimate downstream latency/cost. Can we expose traffic_split as both metric and an API endpoint?

sam: we can emit traffic_split_percentage as a metric, and expose an internal read-only API that returns the last N windows per region. Simulation in the console would call that API and run a weighted projection using historical latency percentiles. Might need a lightweight job to compute weighted projections so the UI isn't doing heavy ops.

maya: good. For the failover panel we also want a small timeline of routing decisions (timestamped events) so PMs can click a spike and see which requests were rerouted. Something like: `routing.events` stream with event_type=fallback|degraded|recovered.

observability-bot: reminder — new metrics must follow naming and tag conventions (team: telemetry). See docs: https://go/redwood-metrics-guide. Submit metric PR and schema before instrumentation.

priya: action items: 1) sam to open metric PR listing names+labels+units; 2) eng-platform (maya) to draft dashboard wireframe + panels list; 3) eng-sre (priya) to define SLO thresholds and alert rules; 4) product (alex) to mock console interactions for traffic-split simulation.

sam: I'll open the PR today. Quick question — for region-level p99 do we want aggregated across model_variants or split by variant? p99 can be noisy if split by small variants.

maya: prefer both: aggregated p99 for the region and variant-sliced p99 for top-3 variants by QPS. Add a config flag so dashboard only shows variant breakdown when variant QPS > X.

alex: UX OK. For tiles, recommend small-sparkline + current value + delta vs baseline. For heatmap, color by p95 (not p99) to avoid constant red.

priya: one more — include a synthetic probe metric for each region that simulates a short prompt to the model and measures cold-start tail. Useful for detecting cross-region capacity issues.

sam: noted. I'll add `redwood.synthetic.probe_latency_ms{region,zone}`.

maya: thanks all. I'll create a confluence doc with proposed panels and link to sam's PR once it's up. Ping me when the metric PR is ready so we can schedule a short sync with product and SRE. :thumbsup:

alex: removing blockers: if we get the metrics by EOD tomorrow we can schedule a 30m demo next week.

observability-bot: deployment note — metrics with high cardinality (model_variant + zone + pool) flagged. Please keep variant label cardinality bounded (suggest top-N only).

maya: ack. we'll follow top-3 variant rule. Thanks everyone.
